subject: Re: Equinity RFI — control mapping & evidence onboarding
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@equinity.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@equinity.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Equinity RFI — initial control list and evidence asks

Hi Michael / Laura,

Thanks for taking our RFI. Attached is the high-level control list we pulled from our SIG/ISO questionnaire — the Equinity security team flagged ~42 items where they want explicit artifacts and control owners. Two asks to start: (1) an initial control crosswalk showing Redwood controls mapped to our SIG control IDs, and (2) a timeline for producing evidence samples (policies, runbooks, logs, config snapshots).

We prefer a two-week sprint cadence for initial delivery and will take staged handoffs (sensitive items first).

Files attached: equinity_rfi_controls_v1.xlsx (control list), sample_questionnaire.pdf

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Vendor Assurance — Equinity Capital
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@equinity.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Equinity RFI — initial control list and evidence asks

Sophie — thanks, received.

Quick plan: we can deliver a first-pass control crosswalk and an evidence manifest within 5 business days, and then operate on a prioritized two-week sprint to hand off artifacts you flagged as high priority (encryption/keyproof, access control, change management, and audit logs). Attaching our initial crosswalk (equinity_control_crosswalk.xlsx) — it maps Equinity SIG IDs to Redwood control names and the primary artifact types we’ll provide.

Notes (high level):
- Where Equinity asks for SOC 2 control substantiation, we’ll provide policy + sample logs + configuration snapshots.
- For ISO-specific reqs (Annex A items), we’ll provide process runbooks and the relevant SOC/ISO attestations.
- We will not include raw production secrets or customer payload in any artifact; logs will be redacted samples and telemetry extracts.

Marissa — can you own collection for the encryption/key rotation artifacts (KMS rotation report, key custody list)? Laura — can you coordinate the audit-log sample and the app config snapshot?

Sophie / Tom — if that plan works, confirm the top 8 control IDs you want prioritized and we’ll kick off the sprint.

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Director, Customer Assurance — Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@equinity.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@equinity.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Feb 2027 10:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Equinity RFI — initial control list and evidence asks

Michael/Team —

Thanks for the quick reply and the crosswalk. A few clarifying items from our side before you start:

1) Control Evidence Format: For audit logs, can you provide CSV extracts with field-level descriptions (timestamp, event_type, actor_id, resource, result)? We’ll ingest into our evidence tracker.
2) KMS Proof: we need a signed report or KMS rotation spreadsheet (dates + rotation IDs) covering the last 12 months for production keys.
3) Third-party controls: for hosted infra (GCP/Azure) are you providing the third-party attestations or do we need to request them separately?

Priority list to start (top 8): SIG-A1 (Access provisioning), SIG-K3 (Encryption & key lifecycle), SOC2-CC6 (Audit logging), SIG-M2 (Change management), ISO-A.9.2 (user access management), SIG-T1 (Data retention / deletion), SOC2-CC5 (Monitoring & alerts), SIG-P4 (Vendor risk management).

Let us know the expected delivery date for each artifact.

-Tom
Tom Reynolds
Security Assurance — Equinity Capital
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@equinity.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@equinity.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Equinity RFI — initial control list and evidence asks

Tom / Sophie —

Thanks for the priorities. Below is the artifact plan and delivery timeline (two-week sprint increments). We will provide redacted, review-ready artifacts and a manifest describing redaction scopes and collection methods.

Sprint 1 (deliver by 2027-02-09):
- SIG-A1 (Access provisioning): user provisioning/deprovisioning policy (policy_access_v1.pdf), sample provisioning ticket export (user_provisioning_sample.csv), change log excerpt.
- SIG-K3 (Encryption & key lifecycle): KMS rotation summary (kms_rotation_report.pdf), key custody owners (key_custody_list.csv) — Marissa will attach.
- SOC2-CC6 (Audit logging): log schema + CSV extract (audit_log_sample.csv) + field map (audit_field_map.md).

Sprint 2 (deliver by 2027-02-23):
- SIG-M2 (Change management): change policy (change_mgmt_policy.pdf), recent change tickets export (change_tickets_last90.csv).
- ISO-A.9.2 (user access management): access review evidence (access_review_2026Q4.pdf).
- SIG-T1 (Data retention / deletion): retention policy + deletion workflow (retention_policy.pdf, deletion_playbook.md).

Sprint 3 (deliver by 2027-03-08):
- SOC2-CC5 (Monitoring & alerts): monitoring runbook, sample alert traces.
- SIG-P4 (Vendor risk management): vendor inventory + third-party attestations index (vendor_index.csv).

Third-party attestations: we will attach relevant cloud provider SOC/ISO packages and include links to public attestations. If Equinity needs Redwood to fetch any proprietary partner reports, confirm which vendors and we’ll include that as an add-on.

Marissa — I’ve added action items in the shared drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FqX-example-link). Marissa will upload the KMS artifacts and the evidence manifest (redwood_evidence_manifest_v1.zip).

Sophie / Tom — can you confirm Sprint 1 acceptance criteria? Specifically: sample audit log format (CSV w/ 6 fields), KMS report (rotation entries for last 12 months), and provisioning sample includes user_id + role + created_at fields.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Assurance Manager — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0147
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@equinity.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@equinity.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Equinity RFI — initial control list and evidence asks

Sophie / Tom —

Following up to confirm we will: deliver Sprint 1 artifacts by COB 2027-02-09 (attached manifest and crosswalk), and begin Sprint 2 work the following Monday. Key commitments:

- Attached: equinity_control_crosswalk.xlsx (mapping), redwood_evidence_manifest_v1.zip (manifest with file list and redaction notes).
- Ownership: Marissa (KMS/keyproofs), Laura (logs & access), Michael (escalations / timelines).
- Acceptance criteria to confirm: CSV schema for audit logs (timestamp, event_type, actor_id, resource, outcome, request_id), KMS rotation entries for last 12 months, provisioning export with user_id/role/created_at.

If you confirm acceptance we’ll mark Sprint 1 complete and share transfer instructions for secure artifact delivery (SFTP link or secure Share). If you prefer DocuSign or an evidence upload to your portal, send the endpoint and we’ll push artifacts there.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Michael Grant
Director, Customer Assurance — Redwood Inference
attachments: equinity_control_crosswalk.xlsx, redwood_evidence_manifest_v1.zip
